# IPQmedia Field Guide

> Marketing and lead generation resources for architecture firms, written by IPQmedia, a client acquisition agency for US architecture firms. Every guide covers both residential firms (clients are homeowners) and commercial firms (clients are developers and business owners), with real data and verified sources.

IPQmedia runs done-for-you paid advertising (primarily Meta) that gets architecture firms qualified client leads on a pay-per-performance basis. Founder: Arseniy Volosevich. Program details: https://beam.ipqmedia.com/program

Canonical URL form for every page below is without a trailing slash. Index of all guides: https://ipqmedia.com/resources

## Core guides

- [Architecture marketing](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing): The 2026 field guide. All seventeen channels an architecture firm can use to win work, what each one actually does, and the order to run them in. The hub every guide below links into.
- [Marketing plan for an architecture firm](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-plan-for-architects): The plan with prices on it. Median cost per lead $51.50 and cost per booked consultation $177.19 across 26 US firm accounts over the twelve months to 17 Nov 2026; a median full month of spend was $1,529 for 24 leads. Also documents that Google's AI Overview attributes a "5 to 10 percent of revenue" budget rule to sources that do not contain it (three of four checked at the publisher on 16 September 2026).
- [How often architects should change their Facebook ads](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/facebook-ad-fatigue-for-architects): 418 Facebook and Instagram ads across 20 US architecture firm accounts, Mar to Oct 2026. The best ad produced 50% of an account's leads at the median; long-running winners lost about 12% efficiency after week 8; ads with no lead after $100 went on to $156 per lead against $40.
- [Consultation booking for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/consultation-booking-for-architects): 1,194 consultations booked with 25 US architecture firms over 12 months. 74% of self-booked consultations were booked outside weekday office hours, 29% on weekends; 41% were held within 24 hours of booking; Monday is the busiest meeting day.
- [Lead generation for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/lead-generation-for-architects): How architecture firms get qualified client inquiries on purpose instead of waiting on referrals.
- [Meta ads for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/meta-ads-for-architects): Why Facebook and Instagram ads are the demand engine for both residential and commercial firms.
- [Marketing for residential architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-residential-architects): Reaching homeowners planning a build or major renovation. Builder searches outnumber architect searches about 25 to 1 for a custom home; 78.5% of 1,644 residential Meta leads (16 firms, to Nov 2026) planned a new home; residential $108.47 vs commercial $89.09 per booked consultation (Nov 2026 benchmark).
- [Marketing for commercial architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-commercial-architects): Reaching developers, business owners and facilities directors, with first-party data on 208 commercial leads from Meta ads at three US architecture firms (Aug-Oct 2026): middle stated budget $3 million, 36.5% booked a consultation against 17.1% for residential leads at the same firms, booking rate by project type.

## Channel guides

- [AI search for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/ai-search-for-architects): What ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude actually cite when a client asks how to hire an architect. 275 cited sources logged across 16 answers on 10 September 2026: 63% came from a practice's own website, 10% from directories and marketplaces, 9% from professional associations. All 39 resolvable firm URLs were guide pages, none were portfolios. Plus our own referral data (Jul-Nov 2026): 20 real people arrived from AI engines (19 ChatGPT), 8 landed on a guide, 1 booked a call.
- [SEO for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/seo-for-architects): Organic search as the compounding layer, with 16 weeks of our own Search Console data (Jul-Oct 2026) on how long ranking takes.
- [Google Ads for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/google-ads-for-architects): Google's own November 2026 click and volume data for eight architect searches: searches down 21.5% Jan-Oct 2026 vs 2025 ("residential architect" the one riser, +25%), click estimates up on 7 of 8 ("commercial architect" $15.12 to $18.63), and a check of what ChatGPT and Perplexity quote firms for Google Ads (three of eight answers said up to $40 a click, a price Google's data shows for none of these searches).
- [Google Business Profile for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/google-business-profile-for-architects): The map pack as a free capture layer. Review counts behind the pack in 12 US metros (Oct 2026), and a November re-run: 18 of 36 slots changed hands in 38 days, and "commercial architect near me" shared 20 of 36 slots with the generic search.
- [Content marketing for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/content-marketing-for-architects): What to publish, measured from who AI engines cite on four buyer questions (Sep 2026: commercial firm selection 18 of 22 cited pages from practices, developer selection 0 practice pages written for developers), plus Orbit Media 2026 blogging survey benchmarks.
- [Email marketing for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/email-marketing-for-architects): Follow-up and nurture, where most inquiries are lost. Includes 2,026 architecture-firm leads by stated project start (40.7% six months or more) and booking rate by timeline (Oct 2026).
- [LinkedIn for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/linkedin-for-architects): A real channel for commercial firms, a staff room for residential ones, with Edelman-LinkedIn survey data and what 16 AI answers on hiring an architect said about LinkedIn (0 of 16 sent buyers there).
- [Social media for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/social-media-for-architects): What posting actually produces. Across 24.4 million Instagram posts, single-image reach fell 21.96% in a year while brands published 24.04% more. Across 21 IPQmedia-run architecture firm ad accounts over twelve months, a median account needs roughly 680 impressions per lead at a median $50 cost per lead. Brand-search check on 28 map-pack firms (12 Nov 2026): Google showed the firm's own Instagram or Facebook on page one for 12 of 27 and its AI Overview cited them in 11 of 21; ChatGPT and Perplexity cited Instagram or Facebook 0 times in 636 citations. Of 123 leads where the app was recorded, 92 came through Facebook, 31 through Instagram.
- [Houzz for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/houzz-for-architects): Whether Houzz advertising is worth it for an architecture firm. Houzz does not publish its ad pricing. Houzz's own 2026 study of 20,000+ users found 27% of renovating homeowners planning to spend under $10,000 and 17% over $100,000; among 1,760 Meta ad leads at 15 architecture firms (Jul-Nov 2026), 66.9% named a budget band starting at $100,000+. Houzz was 4 of 275 sources in 16 AI answers to architect-selection questions, never an architect's profile.
- [RFPs for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/rfp-for-architects): Where architecture RFPs get posted, why public agencies must select on qualifications rather than fee, the Deltek 2026 median capture rate of 44.4% across 896 firms, the lowest since 2019, and what 8 AI answers tell developers about hiring an architect (0 of 8 mention an RFP).
- [Referral systems for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/referral-systems-for-architects): Turning word of mouth from luck into a system, with the referral partners and repeat developers found in 308 booking notes across 25 firms, BrightLocal 2026 on AI recommendations, and what AIA and NCARB rules say about referral fees.
- [Partnerships for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/partnerships-for-architects): Standing arrangements with realtors, builders, developers and design-builders.
- [Direct mail for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/direct-mail-for-architects): A warm-list follow-up layer, not a discovery engine. USPS 2025 survey: 25% of ad mail from a known business rated very likely to get a response vs 3% from strangers; only 3 of 2,196 architecture-firm leads gave a street address (Sep 2025-Oct 2026).
- [PR and press for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/pr-and-press-for-architects): Press and awards as a credibility layer. Includes what 16 AI answers to four architect-selection questions cited (Sep 2026: 0 of 275 sources from design press, awards mentioned in 2 of 16 answers), Nielsen trust figures (editorial 67%, branded websites 69%) and Muck Rack's 2026 journalist survey on pitches.
- [Website design for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/website-design-for-architects): Fixing the portfolio that doesn't convert, plus what four AI engines tell buyers to check before they call an architect, and who those engines quote on architect fees (Sept 2026 pull).
- [Video marketing for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/video-marketing-for-architects): Film as ad creative first, owned library second. October 2026 pull: YouTube videos were 20 of 74 sources cited in Google AI Overviews across 9 architect marketing queries, median 636 views.
- [Branding for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/branding-for-architects): What a brand fixes, what it cannot, and what it costs. Includes what ChatGPT and Perplexity said about 28 map-pack firms (Nov 2026): 43% and 30% of citations from the firms' own sites, Houzz in 17 of 28 ChatGPT answers, 1 of 28 prices taken from the firm's own words.

## Comparisons

- [Meta ads vs Google Ads for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/meta-ads-vs-google-ads-for-architects): Creating demand against capturing it: Google click costs re-pulled Nov 2026, Meta cost per lead and per booked consultation from 26 firm accounts, what ChatGPT and Perplexity recommend (Google first, 6 of 6) against 2,026 Meta leads' stated start dates.
- [Pay per lead vs retainer for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/pay-per-lead-vs-retainer-for-architects): The three ways firms pay for marketing, who carries the risk in each, and first-party data from 12 firms showing 2.5 to 14 leads per booked consultation on the same ad channel.

## Original data and benchmarks

- [Architecture marketing benchmark report 2026](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing-benchmark-report-2026): Third edition, November 2026. Per-firm quartiles from 26 US architecture firm Meta ad accounts over the twelve months to 17 November 2026. Median cost per lead $52 (middle half $30 to $69), cost per booked consultation $136 pooled and $177 at the median firm. Shows what moved since the September edition (impression costs up 14 percent, click-to-lead flat) and retires the claim that spring is the expensive quarter; winter is typically the cheapest.
- [Architecture marketing budget calculator](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing-budget-calculator): Interactive tool. Converts a monthly ad budget into expected leads and booked consultations using the per-account distribution from 26 US architecture firm accounts over the twelve months to 17 Nov 2026 (re-based 2026-11-20). Median $51.50 per lead and $177.19 per booked consultation; $3,000 a month is about 58 leads and 17 booked consultations, middle half 11 to 29. Adjustable by segment (residential $41.51 per lead and 38.3% booked against commercial $46.25 and 51.9%, commercial on 2 accounts), by lead capture (in-platform form $41.84 against own landing page $67.96) and by quarter (median account month: January to March 0.91, April to June 1.08, July to September 0.92, October to December 1.13). Reports a range rather than a single figure and stops at the booked consultation because show-rate data is not reliable. In 5 real budget raises (Oct 2025 to Aug 2026) spend rose 57% and leads 6%, cost per lead up in 4 of 5; Meta's learning threshold (about 50 results a week per ad set) was reached in 1 of 350 account weeks, so it is not the practical minimum budget.
- [Architecture marketing statistics and costs 2026](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing-statistics-and-costs-2026): Market costs roundup. IPQmedia's own median $52 cost per lead, $3.94 per link click and $177 per booked consultation across 26 firm ad accounts ($161,236 of spend, Nov 2025 to Nov 2026), next to AIA/Deltek billings data, Deltek Clarity win rates, PSMJ marketing spend shares, current search click costs, Clutch's Sep 2026 agency and branding price ranges, and a Nov 2026 check finding 0 of 15 architecture marketing agencies publish a price.
- [Architecture client demand by metro 2026](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-client-demand-by-metro-2026): Google search volume and click cost for architect intent across 16 US metros, next to the adjacent trades clients hire instead. Pulled July and November 2026: architect intent 14,110 searches a month against 102,880 for those trades, demand within 10% in 12 of 16 metros while click prices moved more than 20% in 13 of 16, plus month-by-month seasonality (January jump, March peak).

## Firm types

- [Marketing for landscape architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-landscape-architects): Buyers search "landscape designer near me" 14,800 times a month against 3,600 for "landscape architect near me", plus the full 12-month demand curve, its November collapse, a summer and September 2026 that came in below 2025, and cost searches that peak in March.
- [Marketing for high-end residential architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-high-end-residential-architects): Across 13 residential firm ad accounts over 12 months, aiming at wealthy clients did not reliably raise cost per lead; reach was cheaper and per booked consultation the wealth-targeted firms paid $207 against $246. Across 2,027 residential ad leads at 17 firms in 2026, $1M+ budget leads booked 26.7% vs 24.5%, but 40.2% when starting within 3 months and 10.1% when 12+ months out.

## Rankings

- [Best marketing agencies for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/best-marketing-agencies-for-architects): The 2026 ranking. Fifteen agencies reviewed, nine scored on six weighted criteria, six more named, and the firms that rank for the search without serving architects.

## About this guide

- [Arseniy Volosevich, founder of IPQmedia](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/arseniy-volosevich): Author page. Who writes these guides, the five first-party datasets published here and where each came from, why every guide splits residential and commercial, and the full index of published work.
- [Editorial standards](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/editorial-standards): How sources are verified (publisher not aggregator, sample size required, vintage stated, links re-checked weekly), how the first-party ad account data is built and reported, and a dated public log of every correction made to a live page.
